finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the `u` query parameter is passed directly to URI.open (open-uri) with no scheme, host, or IP validation, and the first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and localhost, and read the responses. open-uri follows redirects (http to http/https), so any filtering would be weak anyway.

trace.note: Route `get /rss` is a public Sinatra handler with no auth
params[:u] is passed straight to URI.open and the body is read
First 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned in the response, giving a non-blind read

finding.guards_checked: No validation or allowlist on the path and no auth filter. No before-filter exists in the file. Sibling route /trusted has a host allowlist that this route lacks. /trusted (app.rb:12-16) checked and SAFE: the host is checked against the TRUSTED allowlist on the same parsed URI object that is fetched, and Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. /version (app.rb:18-20) is SAFE: the URL is a constant.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the attacker-controlled params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read in the public `get "/rss"` handler (app.rb:7), and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes, with no validation, allowlist or auth in the file.
